title: Pythagorean theorem
subject: Math
learningGoal: Given the two legs of a right triangle, find the hypotenuse using a² + b² = c².
spokenLines: Okay, let's talk about the Pythagorean theorem.
It only works for right triangles — that little box means a ninety degree angle.
The two shorter sides are called the legs. We call them a and b.
The longest side, across from the right angle, is the hypotenuse. That's c.
The theorem says: a squared plus b squared equals c squared.
So say our legs are three and four. Let's plug them in.
Three squared is nine. Four squared is sixteen.
Add those and we get twenty five.
The square root of twenty five is five. So c equals five.
That's it. Legs three and four give a hypotenuse of five.
